questions.question: Tso Kar wetland has been included in Ramsar Site in December 2020. In which of the following states or union territories is it located?
questions.questionHtml: Tso Kar wetland has been included in Ramsar Site in December 2020. In which of the following states or union territories is it located?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Ladakh.

Key Points 

  • India has added Tso Kar Wetland Complex in Ladakh as its 42nd Ramsar site, which is the second one in the Union Territory (UT) of Ladakh.
  • The Tso Kar Basin is a high-altitude wetland complex, consisting of two principal waterbodies, Startsapuk Tso, a freshwater lake of about 438 hectares to the south, and Tso Kar itself, a hypersaline lake of 1800 hectares to the north, situated in the Changthang region of Ladakh, India.
    • It is called Tso Kar, meaning white lake, because of the white salt efflorescence found on the margins due to the evaporation of highly saline water.
  • The Tso Kar Basin is an A1 Category Important Bird Area (IBA) as per BirdLife International and a key staging site in the Central Asian Flyway.
  • The site is also one of the most important breeding areas of the Black-necked Crane (Grus nigricollis) in India.
    • This IBA is also the major breeding area for Great Crested Grebe (Podicepscristatus), Bar-headed Geese (Anserindicus), Ruddy Shelduck (Tadornaferruginea), Brown-headed Gull (Larusbrunnicephalus), Lesser Sand-Plover (Charadriusmongolus), and many other species.

Additional Information 

  • The aim of the Ramsar list is “to develop and maintain an international network of wetlands which are important for the conservation of global biological diversity and for sustaining human life through the maintenance of their ecosystem components, processes, and benefits”.
  • Wetlands provide a wide range of important resources and ecosystem services such as food, water, fibre, groundwater recharge, water purification, flood moderation, erosion control and climate regulation.
    • They are, in fact a major source of water and our main supply of freshwater comes from an array of wetlands that help soak rainfall and recharge groundwater.
    • The Ministry of Environment, Forest & Climate Change would be working closely with the UT Wetland Authority to ensure wise use of this site.

questions.question: ______ is a naturally occurring phenomenon that is responsible for the heating of the Earth’s surface and atmosphere.
questions.questionHtml: ______ is a naturally occurring phenomenon that is responsible for the heating of the Earth’s surface and atmosphere.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Greenhouse effect.

Key Points

  • The greenhouse effect is a process that occurs when gases in Earth's atmosphere trap the Sun's heat.
  • This process makes Earth much warmer than it would be without an atmosphere.
  • A greenhouse is a building with glass walls and a glass roof and used to grow plants.
  • It leads to an increase in the Earth's temperature because the glass walls of the greenhouse trap the Sun's heat.

Additional Information 

  • Radiation is the energy that comes from a source and travels through space at the speed of light like heat, light, ultraviolet rays, etc.
  • The increase in the Earth's average temperature over the past few decades is called Global warming.
  • Global warming occurs when carbon dioxide (CO2) and other air pollutants and greenhouse gases are collected in the atmosphere and absorb sunlight and solar radiation that have bounced off the earth’s surface.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about the ionosphere is NOT correct?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following statements about the ionosphere is NOT correct?

options.text: Radio waves transmitted from the earth are reflected back to the earth by this layer.
options.html: Radio waves transmitted from the earth are reflected back to the earth by this layer.

options.text: It is ionized by solar and cosmic radiation.
options.html: It is ionized by solar and cosmic radiation.

options.text: It is located immediately above the stratopause.
options.html: It is located immediately above the stratopause.

questions.solution:
The Ionosphere is the ionized part of Earth's upper atmosphere, which extends from about 60 km to 1,000 km altitude.

  • The ionosphere is a very active part of the atmosphere, and it grows and shrinks depending on the energy it absorbs from the Sun.
  • It contains charged particles and is ionized by solar radiation.
  • The ionosphere is a region that includes the thermosphere and parts of the mesosphere and exosphere.

questions.question: DDT adversely affects our environment because:
questions.questionHtml: DDT adversely affects our environment because:

options.text: it can kill beneficial insects like honey bees
options.html: it can kill beneficial insects like honey bees

options.text: it can allow growth of harmful insects
options.html: it can allow growth of harmful insects

options.text: it can promote growth of harmful insects
options.html: it can promote growth of harmful insects

questions.solution:
The correct answer is it can kill beneficial insects like honey bees.

Key Points

  • DDT is very insoluble in water and very persistent in the environment, making it a highly polluting hazard.
  • Its half-life has been reported to be between 2 and 15 years.
  • DDT (dichloro-diphenyl-trichloroethane) was developed as the first of the modern synthetic insecticides in the 1940s.
  • It was initially used with great effect to combat malaria, typhus, and other insect-borne human diseases among both military and civilian populations.

Additional Information

  • Insecticides are chemicals used to control insects by killing them or preventing them from engaging in undesirable or destructive behaviours.
  • Organic pesticides are usually considered as those pesticides that come from natural sources. 
  • Synthetic contact insecticides are now the primary agents of insect control.​ 
  • Inorganic insecticides are of mineral origin, mainly compounds of antimony, arsenic, barium, boron, copper, fluorine, mercury, selenium, sulfur, thallium, and zinc, and elemental phosphorus and sulfur.

questions.question: Eutrophication is a condition where excessive growth of algal bloom occurs on the surface of a water body because of abundant nutrients. Which of the following are the key nutrients for eutrophication?
questions.questionHtml: Eutrophication is a condition where excessive growth of algal bloom occurs on the surface of a water body because of abundant nutrients. Which of the following are the key nutrients for eutrophication?
questions.solution: Phosphorus and nitrogen are the key nutrients responsible for eutrophication as they promote excessive algal growth in water bodies. Phosphorus enters through agricultural runoff, detergents, and sewage, while nitrogen comes from fertilizers, livestock waste, and industrial discharges. This leads to oxygen depletion, harming aquatic organisms and biodiversity.

questions.question: The process by which a water body gradually becomes enriched with nutrients and minerals, mainly phosphorus and nitrogen, leading to enormous growth of algae on the surface of the water, thus decreasing the amount of dissolved oxygen in the water is known as:
questions.questionHtml: The process by which a water body gradually becomes enriched with nutrients and minerals, mainly phosphorus and nitrogen, leading to enormous growth of algae on the surface of the water, thus decreasing the amount of dissolved oxygen in the water is known as:
questions.solution: Eutrophication is the process where water bodies become nutrient-rich, mainly with phosphorus and nitrogen, often from agricultural runoff, sewage, or industrial waste. This leads to excessive algal blooms, blocking sunlight, and consuming dissolved oxygen during decomposition, creating hypoxic conditions that disrupt aquatic ecosystems and harm marine life.

questions.question: What are the dissolved and suspended impurities in sewage called?
questions.questionHtml: What are the dissolved and suspended impurities in sewage called?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option 4.

Key PointsThe dissolved and suspended impurities in sewage are generally referred to as contaminants or pollutants. Hence, Option 4 is correct.

These can be further categorized into various types, including:

  • Organic matter: Such as human waste, food scraps, and soaps.
  • Nutrients: Including nitrogen and phosphorus compounds, which can promote excessive growth of algae in water bodies (eutrophication).
  • Pathogens: Bacteria, viruses, and parasites that can cause diseases.
  • Chemicals: These can include pharmaceuticals, pesticides, and industrial chemicals.
  • Microplastics: Small plastic particles that persist in the environment.
  • Heavy metals: Such as lead, mercury, and cadmium, which are toxic to aquatic life and humans.

The solid particles that are suspended in wastewater are often referred to as "suspended solids," while the dissolved ones can be nutrients, certain organic compounds, or other soluble materials. Proper treatment of sewage is necessary to remove or reduce these impurities before the water is released back into the environment or reused.

questions.question: ______ refers to a sanitation system in which toilets collect human excreta in sealable, removable cartridges that are transported to treatment facilities.
questions.questionHtml: ______ refers to a sanitation system in which toilets collect human excreta in sealable, removable cartridges that are transported to treatment facilities.
questions.solution:
• Container-based sanitation (CBS) is a sanitation method in which toilets collect human waste and transport it to treatment facilities in sealable, removable containers (also known as cartridges).
  • This method of sanitation entails the use of a commercial service that offers specific types of portable toilets and distributes empty containers when full ones are picked up. The service carries excreta and carefully disposes of or reuses it.
  • The users are normally responsible for the cost of excreta collection. CBS can be utilised to offer low-income urban areas safe collection, transportation, and treatment of faeces at a lesser cost than establishing and maintaining sewers with the right development, support, and collaborations.
  • Sanitation systems based on containers are a low-cost option. They can be employed in quickly increasing cities, refugee camps, and disaster relief circumstances.
  • They are in line with Sustainable Development Goal 6 of the United Nations, which is to "provide sanitation for all by 2030."

questions.question: What does 'C' stand for in ITCZ?
questions.questionHtml: What does 'C' stand for in ITCZ?
questions.solution:
In ITCZ, "C" is stand for Convergence.

  • The Intertropical Convergence Zone (ITCZ) is the zone that covers the Earth, near the equator.
  • Where trade winds from the Northern and Southern Hemispheres come together.
  • The sun and warm water of the equator heat up the air in the ITCZ, increase its temperature, and keep it buoyant.
  • With the aid of the convergence of the industrial winds, the buoyant air is rising.
  • When the air increases, it spreads and cools, releasing concentrated heat in an almost endless cycle of thunderstorms.

questions.question: The condition, when the environment becomes enriched with nutrients, increasing the amount of plant and algae growth in estuaries and coastal waters, is called:
questions.questionHtml: The condition, when the environment becomes enriched with nutrients, increasing the amount of plant and algae growth in estuaries and coastal waters, is called:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is eutrophication.

Key Points

  • Eutrophication is the process by which a body of water becomes overly enriched with nutrients.
  • This enrichment leads to an increase in the growth of plants and algae in the water.
  • Sources of nutrients causing eutrophication include runoff from agriculture, wastewater discharge, and industrial effluents.
  • Algal blooms can deplete the oxygen in the water, leading to dead zones where aquatic life cannot survive.
  • Eutrophication can also result in the deterioration of water quality, affecting both ecosystems and human health.
  • Management practices include reducing nutrient loads, improving wastewater treatment, and implementing sustainable agricultural practices.

 Additional Information

  • Mineralisation
    • Mineralisation refers to the process by which organic matter is decomposed to release inorganic nutrients.
    • This process is crucial for the cycling of nutrients in ecosystems.
  • Ozone depletion
    • Ozone depletion refers to the thinning of the Earth's ozone layer caused by chemicals like chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs).
    • This depletion allows more harmful ultraviolet (UV) radiation to reach the Earth's surface, affecting both human health and the environment.
  • Greenhouse effect
    • The greenhouse effect is the process by which certain gases in the Earth's atmosphere trap heat, leading to an increase in global temperatures.
    • Key greenhouse gases include carbon dioxide (CO2), methane (CH4), and nitrous oxide (N2O).
    • This effect is crucial for maintaining the Earth's temperature but is currently exacerbated by human activities, leading to global warming.

questions.question: A pyramid of biomass is a diagram that shows the population at each level of the food chain. Accordingly, ________ occupy the base with the highest biomass.
questions.questionHtml: A pyramid of biomass is a diagram that shows the population at each level of the food chain. Accordingly, ________ occupy the base with the highest biomass.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is producers.

Key Points

  • A pyramid of biomass is a graphical representation that shows the population at each level of the food chain.
  • Producers occupy the base with the highest biomass.
  • The relationship between numbers, biomass, energy, or bio productivity of an ecosystem can be represented by a pyramid known as the ecological pyramid.
  • The trophic level is the place that a living organism occupies in a food chain.
  • In a biomass pyramid, producers are at the base, followed by herbivores and then carnivores at the top.
  • The pyramid of biomass shows the flow of energy from producers to consumers.
  • 10 percent of the energy gets transferred to the next trophic level and the rest is either utilized for metabolic processes or excreted out.

Additional Information

  • Carnivores that eat herbivores are called secondary consumers.
  • A separate trophic level, the decomposers or transformers, consists of organisms such as bacteria and fungi that break down dead organisms and waste materials into nutrients usable by the producers.
  • Primary consumers make up the second trophic level. They are also called herbivores.

questions.question: Biotic potential can be defined as:
questions.questionHtml: Biotic potential can be defined as:

options.text: the minimum number of individuals of a species that can survive but cannot reproduce
options.html: the minimum number of individuals of a species that can survive but cannot reproduce

options.text: the minimum number of individuals a species can produce
options.html: the minimum number of individuals a species can produce

options.text: the maximum number of individuals a species can produce
options.html: the maximum number of individuals a species can produce

options.text: the maximum number of individuals of a species that cannot survive after birth
options.html: the maximum number of individuals of a species that cannot survive after birth

questions.solution: Biotic potential refers to the maximum reproductive capacity of an organism under optimal conditions, without limiting factors like food scarcity, predation, or disease. This concept is significant in population ecology as it helps understand a species' growth potential. Factors influencing biotic potential include reproduction rate and reproductive lifespan. While idealized, actual population sizes are often lower due to environmental resistance factors such as food availability, predation, and disease. Understanding biotic potential is crucial for conservation and managing species populations, and ecologists use it to model and predict population growth responses to environmental changes.

questions.question: Identify a mobile source of food.
questions.questionHtml: Identify a mobile source of food.
questions.solution: A mobile source of food refers to food that can move from one place to another. Among the options provided, a deer is a living animal that can move, making it a mobile source of food. Other options like grass, dead goat, and shrubs are either stationary or non-living and thus do not qualify as mobile sources of food. Mobile sources of food are significant in the context of predators and hunting in the animal kingdom. Animals like deer can migrate and move to different areas in search of food and water, which makes them mobile. Understanding the mobility of food sources helps in the study of animal behavior and ecology.

questions.question: According to the Central Ground Water Board, BIS (IS_10500 and revised module IS 10500:2012) specifications in the Uniform Drinking Water Quality Monitoring Protocol, what is the acceptable pH value of drinking water specification in India?
questions.questionHtml: According to the Central Ground Water Board, BIS (IS_10500 and revised module IS 10500:2012) specifications in the Uniform Drinking Water Quality Monitoring Protocol, what is the acceptable pH value of drinking water specification in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 6.5 - 8.5.

Key Points

  • According to the Central Ground Water Board, BIS (IS_10500 and revised module IS 10500:2012) specifications in the Uniform Drinking Water Quality Monitoring Protocol, 6.5 - 8.5 is the acceptable pH value of drinking water specification in India.
  • The pH value of water indicates the logarithm of the reciprocal of hydrogen ion concentration present in water.
  • It is thus an indicator of the acidity or the alkalinity of water.
  • Hence, if the pH of water is more than 7, it will be alkaline, and if it is less than 7, it will be acidic.
  • The maximum acidity will be at zero value of pH and the maximum alkalinity will be at a value of pH equal to 14.
  • pH is measured by a potentiometer in which the potential exerted by H+ is measured.
  • It can also be measured by a colour indicator.
  • The Colour formed is compared with the standard colour.
  • Permissible values of pH for public supplies may range from 6.5 to 8.5.

questions.question: Eutrophication can be defined as:
questions.questionHtml: Eutrophication can be defined as:

options.text: the gradual increase in the concentration of phosphorus, nitrogen, and other plant nutrients in an grassland ecosystem
options.html: the gradual increase in the concentration of phosphorus, nitrogen, and other plant nutrients in an grassland ecosystem

options.text: the gradual decrease in the concentration of phosphorus, nitrogen, and other plant nutrients in an aging aquatic ecosystem such as a lake
options.html: the gradual decrease in the concentration of phosphorus, nitrogen, and other plant nutrients in an aging aquatic ecosystem such as a lake

options.text: the gradual increase in the concentration of phosphorus, nitrogen, and other plant nutrients in desert areas
options.html: the gradual increase in the concentration of phosphorus, nitrogen, and other plant nutrients in desert areas

options.text: the gradual increase in the concentration of phosphorus, nitrogen, and other plant nutrients in an aging aquatic ecosystem such as a lake
options.html: the gradual increase in the concentration of phosphorus, nitrogen, and other plant nutrients in an aging aquatic ecosystem such as a lake

questions.solution: Eutrophication is the gradual increase in phosphorus, nitrogen, and other plant nutrients in aging aquatic ecosystems like lakes, leading to algae and aquatic plant growth that depletes oxygen and harms aquatic life. It is primarily caused by agricultural runoff and wastewater. Consequences include harmful algal blooms, fish kills, and biodiversity loss. Management practices to mitigate eutrophication include reducing nutrient runoff and improving wastewater treatment. Natural occurrences of eutrophication are slow, but human activities accelerate it. Preventative measures include sustainable agriculture, phosphate-free detergents, and wetland protection. Public awareness is crucial for addressing nutrient pollution impacts.

questions.question: Consider following statements. 1) A system consisting of biotic and abiotic components is known as ecosystem. 2) All the components of the ecosystem are inter-related. 3) Ecosystem always have clear boundaries. Which statement is/are correct?
questions.questionHtml:
Consider following statements.

1) A system consisting of biotic and abiotic components is known as ecosystem. 

2) All the components of the ecosystem are inter-related.

3) Ecosystem always have clear boundaries.

Which statement is/are correct?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Both 1 and 2 statements are correct.

Key Points

Ecosystem: 

  • All organisms such as plants, animals, microorganisms and human beings as well as the physical surroundings interact with each other and maintain a balance in nature.
  • All the interacting organisms in an area together with the non-living constituents of the environment form an ecosystem.
  • The term ecosystem was coined by Tansley.

Additional Information

Explanation:

Components of an ecosystem:

Biotic Components: 

  • It includes producers, consumers and decomposers.
  • All living things have a direct or indirect influence on other organisms in an environment.
  • Example: plants, animals, humans, microorganism etc.

Abiotic components: 

  • All the in-organic components of the ecosystem, non-living physical and chemical composition of nature are abiotic components.
  • Example: land, stones, water, humus (organic waste), air etc.

questions.question: In an ecosystem, vertical distribution of different species occupying different levels is called ______.

Tropical rainforests have the highest species composition. Standing crop indicates productivity, with forests having high amounts and grasslands and arid regions having low amounts.

questions.solution: Ecology is the science that studies the relationships between living organisms and their environment. questions.question: Who is best known for his testimony on climate change to congressional committees in the 1980 s, Which helped raise wider awareness of the global warming issue?
questions.questionHtml: Who is best known for his testimony on climate change to congressional committees in the 1980 s, Which helped raise wider awareness of the global warming issue?
questions.solution: James Hansen is renowned for his influential testimony on climate change to congressional committees in the 1980s, which significantly raised awareness about global warming. As a climate scientist and former director of the NASA Goddard Institute for Space Studies, Hansen's testimony emphasized the critical need to reduce greenhouse gas emissions. His work has been pivotal in understanding the human impact on climate and has shaped both public policy and scientific research. Hansen's 1988 testimony asserted with high certainty that global warming was occurring due to human activities, advocating for immediate action to mitigate climate change.

questions.question: In which of the following Tiger Reserves of India, is its first hot air balloon wildlife safari launched in December 2020?
questions.questionHtml: In which of the following Tiger Reserves of India, is its first hot air balloon wildlife safari launched in December 2020?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Bandhavgarh Tiger Reserve.

Key Points

  • India's first hot air balloon safari in a tiger reserve was launched on December 25, 2020, in Madhya Pradesh's world-famous Bandhavgarh Tiger Reserve.
    • The safari was launched by Madhya Pradesh forest minister Vijay Shah.
  • During the launch, the Minister said that the hot air balloon wildlife safari will be restricted to the buffer area, from where the tourists will be able to watch leopards, tigers, Indian sloth bears, and other wild animals. 
  • The service will be operated by a Jaipur-based company Sky Waltz.

Additional Information

  • Dudhwa National Park.
    • The Dudhwa Tiger Reserve is a protected area in Uttar Pradesh located on the India-Nepal border.
    • The Dudhwa National Park has a number of species of birds, reptiles, wild elephants, aquatic animals, one-horned rhinos, wild elephants besides its enriched flora and fauna. Its undisturbed natural forest cover, vast spans of grasslands, and wetlands.
    • It is the only place in U.P. where both Tigers and Rhinos can be spotted together.
  • Jim Corbett National Park is a forested wildlife sanctuary in northern India’s Uttarakhand State.
    • Rich in flora and fauna, it’s known for its Bengal tigers. Animals, including tigers, leopards and wild elephants, roam the Dhikala zone.
    • On the banks of the Ramganga Reservoir, the Sonanadi zone is home to elephants and leopards, along with hundreds of species of birds.
  • Manas National Park ' is a national park, UNESCO Natural World Heritage site, a Project Tiger reserve, an elephant reserve and a biosphere reserve in Assam, India.
    • Located in the Himalayan foothills, it is contiguous with the Royal Manas National Park in Bhutan.

questions.question: Which ecologist’s research provided revolutionary new insights into how energy and nutrients move through the ecosystems?
questions.questionHtml: Which ecologist’s research provided revolutionary new insights into how energy and nutrients move through the ecosystems?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Raymond L Lindeman.

Key Points

  • Raymond Laurel Lindeman (1915 – June 29, 1942) was an ecologist whose graduate research is credited with being a seminal study in the field of ecosystem ecology, specifically on the topic of trophic dynamics.
  • Lindeman completed his Ph.D. at the University of Minnesota with his thesis work being concerned with the history and ecological dynamics of Cedar Bog Lake.
  • Some insights of his research:
    • Energy is passed from one trophic level to the next trophic level.
    • Hence, energy flows in one direction through successive trophic levels in a food chain.
    • Nutrients are produced from the matter. The matter may be organic or inorganic.
    • The organic and inorganic matter is produced, exchanged, and moved within the ecosystem and this is called cycling.

Additional Information

  • Sir Arthur George Tansley FLS, FRS (15 August 1871 – 25 November 1955) was an English botanist and a pioneer in the science of ecology.
  • Ernst Heinrich Philipp August Haeckel was a German zoologist, naturalist, eugenicist, philosopher, physician, professor, marine biologist, and artist.
  • Charles Sutherland Elton FRS (29 March 1900 – 1 May 1991) was an English zoologist and animal ecologist.

questions.question: In which year was the National Biodiversity Authority, a statutory autonomous body, established under the Ministry of Environment and Forests, Government of India?
questions.questionHtml: In which year was the National Biodiversity Authority, a statutory autonomous body, established under the Ministry of Environment and Forests, Government of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 2003.

Key Points

  • National Biodiversity Authority
    • After signing the Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD) in 1992, India formed the National Biodiversity Authority (NBA), a statutory autonomous organisation under the Ministry of Environment, Forests, and Climate Change, in 2003.
    • It was made to carry out the requirements of the Biological Diversity Act, 2002.
    • It serves as facilitation, regulation, and advisory body to the Indian government "on issues of conservation, sustainable use of biological resources, and fair and equitable distribution of benefits emerging from the use of biological resources."
    • Its main office is in Chennai, India.
    • Additionally, it provides guidance to State Governments in designating biodiversity hotspots as heritage monuments.
    • NBA held the first-ever National Biodiversity Congress (NBC) in Thiruvananthapuram, Kerala, in 2012. 

Additional Information

  • Since its founding, NBA has supported the development of State Biodiversity Boards (SBBs) in 29 States and aided the construction of approximately 1,39,831 Biodiversity Management Committees (BMCs).
  • The National Biodiversity Authority is charged with controlling access to biological resources and/or related knowledge for research, bio-survey, and commercial use, as well as obtaining intellectual property rights, transferring research findings, and transferring accessed biological resources.
  • On the website of the National Biodiversity Authority there are the details of the application forms for Access and Benefit Sharing (ABS) of particular activities.
  • The current chairperson of NBA is Dr. V. B. Mathur.

questions.question: What was the magnitude of the Indian Ocean Tsunami 2004?
questions.questionHtml: What was the magnitude of the Indian Ocean Tsunami 2004?
questions.solution: The Sumatra-Andaman earthquake, also known as the Indian Ocean tsunami or Christmas Day tsunami, occurred in 2004. It was estimated to have released energy equivalent to 23,000 Hiroshima-type atomic bombs. The magnitude 9.1 quake struck 150 miles from the coast of Sumatra island and ruptured a 900-mile stretch of fault line where the Indian and Australian tectonic plates meet. It was a powerful megathrust quake, occurring where a heavy ocean plate slips under a lighter continental plate. The Richter scale, developed by Charles F. Richter in 1934, was used to measure the earthquake's magnitude based on the amplitude of the largest wave recorded on a specific type of seismometer and the distance between the earthquake and the seismometer. The correct answer is 9.1.

questions.question: Which of the following is the best definition of ecological efficiency?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following is the best definition of ecological efficiency?

options.text: The amount of energy utilised at different trophic levels in a food chain
options.html: The amount of energy utilised at different trophic levels in a food chain

options.text: The amount of energy stored at different trophic levels in a food chain
options.html: The amount of energy stored at different trophic levels in a food chain

options.text: The ratio between the mass and the energy flow at different trophic levels in a food chain
options.html: The ratio between the mass and the energy flow at different trophic levels in a food chain

options.text: The ratio between energy flows at different points in a food chain
options.html: The ratio between energy flows at different points in a food chain

questions.solution:
The correct answer is The ratio between energy flows at different points in a food chain.

Key Points

  • Ecological efficiency refers to the efficiency with which energy is transferred from one trophic level to the next in a food chain.
  • Typically, only about 10% of the energy at one trophic level is passed on to the next level; this is known as the 10% law.
  • This concept helps in understanding the energy dynamics and the structure of ecosystems.
  • Higher trophic levels receive less energy, which explains why there are typically fewer organisms at higher levels in a food chain.

Additional Information

  • Trophic Levels
    • In ecology, a trophic level is the position that an organism occupies in a food chain.
    • Primary producers (plants) are at the first trophic level, primary consumers (herbivores) at the second, secondary consumers (carnivores that eat herbivores) at the third, and so on.
  • Energy Flow
    • Energy flow in an ecosystem is one-way: from the sun to producers, then to consumers, and finally to decomposers.
    • Energy is lost at each trophic level, primarily as heat resulting from metabolism.
  • 10% Law
    • The 10% law states that only about 10% of the energy at one trophic level is transferred to the next trophic level.
    • This rule was first introduced by Raymond Lindeman in 1942.
  • Food Chain
    • A food chain is a linear sequence of organisms through which nutrients and energy pass as one organism eats another.
    • In a food chain, each organism occupies a different trophic level.
